newsitem.title: GABON: Fresh delay at Congo Brazzaville talks.
newsitem.headline: Fresh delay at Congo Brazzaville talks.

text.p: Mediators failed to bring the Congo Republic's warring parties face-to-face in Gabon on Wednesday but held out hope of such a meeting on Thursday.
With a truce holding in the Congo capital Brazzaville, U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun said envoys of the two sides had been presented with a draft accord offering a range of options.

"We are waiting for the delegations' reaction to this document tomorrow and we hope that then a debate will take place among all the delegations in the presence of the mediation committee," he told reporters.

Sahnoun and Gabon's veteran president, Omar Bongo, who ended similar ethnic and political clashes that killed 2,000 people after a disputed 1993 parliamentary election, held separate talks with delegation heads on Wednesday.
President Pascal Lissouba and his predecessor and rival Denis Sassou Nguesso remained in Brazzaville.

Sassou's radio there said the sticking point was a decision by the oil-producing former French colony's Constitutional Council to extend Lissouba's mandate until elections can be held. His mandate ends at the end of August.
The council cancelled a planned July 27 presidential election. Sassou did not object to that but wants a government of national salvation.
The showdown began on June 5 after the army surrounded Sassou's home as part of a crackdown on private militias.
